sections: Scales & technical work

All from memory, legato, hands together one octave apart unless stated. Scales (similar motion, 3 octaves): C, G, D, A, E, B, F, Bb, Eb, Ab majors; A, E, B, D, G, C, F minors (harmonic or melodic). Contrary motion from and to the unison (2 octaves): C, E and Eb majors. Chromatic scales from any note named by the examiner, each hand separately, 3 octaves. Arpeggios: major and minor common chords of C, G, D, A, E, B, F, root position, each hand separately, 3 octaves.
Sight-reading

(i) Sight-reading in simple time in C, G, D, A, E, F, Bb or Eb major or A, E, B, D, G or C minor. (ii) Figured bass: 5-6 chords over a bass in C, G or F major, using 5/3 chords on degrees 1-6 and 6/3 on degree 3.
Aural & other tests

Aural: (A) sing or play back a melody within an octave (up to 3 sharps/flats); (B) sing five notes from score in free time (C, F or G major); (C) questions on two features (one of dynamics, articulation, tempo, tonality; plus character) and clap back the rhythm of an extract, identifying 2/3/4 time. Details in ABRSM aural tests section (pp. 94, 96).
